comparator.name: UCR Liberal Arts and Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 Education and Examination Regulations specify 180 EC, Personal & Professional Development in the first year, at least 45 EC of advanced work, and a Liberal Arts & Sciences Portfolio and Reflection. The advanced requirement can be fulfilled with six 7.5 EC courses or with four advanced courses and a 15 EC Research Seminar in the third year. Each regular advanced course includes research. The BA or BSc and any cluster-specific major depend on course choice. The 180 EC on the left show the general degree requirements. The three examples use regular advanced courses.
components: Complete this 7.5 EC course before the third semester.
Complete six 7.5 EC courses at the 300 level, or four such courses and a 15 EC Research Seminar in the third year.
Choose 127.5 EC of other courses, following the applicable prerequisites.

core: A student-designed Liberal Arts and Sciences curriculum combining sciences, social sciences and humanities
Breadth with progressive depth across introductory, intermediate and advanced study
Research, critical thinking, communication and reflective academic development
adjacent: Data science, computer science, mathematics and intelligent systems
Environment, sustainability, ecology and delta challenges
Government, law, history, philosophy and society
Health, cognition, psychology, behaviour and life science
Media, culture, communication, literature and heritage
questions: How can perspectives from different disciplines illuminate complex social problems?
How can data, computation and intelligent systems help address real problems?
How do health, environment, institutions, culture and enterprise shape human futures?

alternatives.label: Liberal Arts & Sciences: Society, Science & Culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum draws substantially from all six UCR clusters and combines social inquiry, science, data, business, health, media and sustainability rather than presenting one cluster as the entire degree.
alternatives.concept: Explore questions about people, institutions and the environment through psychology, politics, sustainability, business, data and media. Build skills in statistical and qualitative research, then apply them in studies of cognition, environmental policy and history.
progression: Sustainability Essentials, Brain & Behavior, rhetoric and programming start the plan. Early methods and comparative politics support later sustainability governance, EU politics, cognition, econometrics and historical research.

alternatives.label: Business Strategy, Markets & Entrepreneurship
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by business foundations, entrepreneurship, finance, economics, leadership, marketing and organisational decisions, with data and programming support.
alternatives.concept: Study how businesses develop products, understand customers and make decisions in changing markets. Connect entrepreneurship and leadership with finance, economics and law, and use data to investigate business questions.
progression: Entrepreneurship, introductory economics and accounting precede finance, strategy and policy work. Statistics precedes econometrics, and the market-research project supplies evidence-gathering experience before final-year marketing.
alternatives.distinctness: 15 courses differ in each direction from the broad example. The business plan adds sustained study of finance, economics, entrepreneurship and leadership.

alternatives.label: Data Science, AI & Autonomous Systems
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum contains a sustained sequence in programming, databases, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, optimisation, robotics, mathematics and statistics.
alternatives.concept: Learn to organise data and build computational models. Progress from programming and mathematics to machine learning, then apply these tools to robotics, computer vision and systems that learn by interacting with their environment. Examine the ethical choices behind those systems.
progression: Programming and discrete mathematics precede algorithms and software development. Calculus and linear algebra support numerical methods and robotics. Probability and machine learning precede decision-making in AI, and these courses prepare students for reinforcement learning and neural networks.
alternatives.distinctness: 19 courses differ in each direction from the broad example and 19 from the business example. The data science plan adds sustained work in algorithms, mathematics, software and AI.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the two generic programme-wide interests and demonstrates the defining cross-cluster Liberal Arts and Sciences model. All remaining generator-eligible interests are assigned to one of the six current official academic clusters. Business & Entrepreneurship and Data Science & Intelligent Systems are considered next in the official cluster order and both pass the evidence, coherence, distinctness and feasibility gates, so they are included as alternatives two and three. Environment & Sustainability, Government & Society, Health, Cognition & Behavior and Media, Culture & Communication are also coherent but cannot be added after the maximum of three alternatives is reached. Every schedule contains exactly 24 courses/180 EC, satisfies prerequisite and term constraints and includes at least six 300-level courses.

notes.text: The left column shows the degree requirements at UCR. The other columns show three ways to choose courses within that same degree.

All students complete a Liberal Arts & Sciences Portfolio and Reflection alongside their courses. Students can meet the advanced requirement through regular 300-level courses or by including a third-year Research Seminar. These examples use regular advanced courses.

audience.programmeDescription: UCR’s English-taught Liberal Arts and Sciences degree lets you combine subjects across six clusters and develop depth in the areas you want to pursue.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The examples show a broad mix across all six clusters, a focus on business and entrepreneurship, and a focus on data science and intelligent systems.
